rules.rule: Check for urgent face symptom conditions
rules.problem: Trigger is the six natural face-complaint findings; every red-box item is checked for, grouped by criterion; eyelid findings come from the 'Manage and refer urgently' line, which is where the page states 'orbital cellulitis likely', so their role is right.

rules.rule: Check for causes of face pain
rules.problem: Follows the Face pain branch (one side -> stabbing/shingles; sinus pattern). Dropped qualifiers noted on c034, c035, c037.

rules.rule: Check for causes of facial weakness
rules.problem: Checks the two Bell's palsy discriminators ('unable to wrinkle forehead or close eye'). 'progressive' is not modelled; harmless.

rules.rule: Check for causes of facial swelling
rules.problem: Painless lips/eyes vs painful swelling with fever/headache/body pain; fever is a routine finding.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible stroke from face symptoms
rules.problem: 'consider stroke' -> possible is right. Three arms match the red-box sentence: forehead-sparing sudden unilateral facial weakness; sudden unilateral facial numbness; any face symptom plus limb weakness/numbness, speech or visual disturbance. Relies on (no Upper facial weakness) evaluating true when the forehead has not been examined, which over-triages rather than under-triages.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible TIA from face symptoms
rules.problem: Identical evidence to the stroke rule, as the page gives one criterion for 'stroke or TIA'.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from face swelling
rules.problem: 'check for anaphylaxis' -> possible is right; and(sudden face/tongue swelling, any of ...) matches the page and the page-20 house pattern, including BP < 90/60 as systolic < 90 or diastolic < 60. Allergen exposure timing dropped (c089-c092).
'facial cellulitis likely' -> probable; painful + red + swollen face + temp >= 38 is exactly the red-box line.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable orbital cellulitis from facial cellulitis
rules.problem: 'orbital cellulitis likely' -> probable; repeats the cellulitis criteria rather than using (active_condition Cellulitis of face), which is equivalent, plus swollen/red/painful eyelid.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable kidney disease from facial swelling
rules.problem: New facial swelling and blood or protein in urine, as on the page.
Unilateral face pain + recurrent severe stabbing facial pain follows the branch; 'superficial' dropped.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable post-herpetic neuralgia of face
rules.problem: Unilateral face pain + history of shingles follows the branch; 'on same side of face' cannot be expressed (c115).

rules.rule: Diagnose probable sinusitis from face pain
rules.problem: All five descriptive features (tenderness, headache, thick/postnasal discharge, recent cold, face pain) are required with 'and'. The page presents them as one descriptive cluster with no 'all of'; a patient with sinus tenderness, positional headache and thick discharge but no recent cold would not get the likely diagnosis. Consider requiring tenderness or headache plus any of the rest, or ask a clinician; also 'worse on bending forward' is lost (c119).
Sudden unilateral facial weakness and (unable to wrinkle forehead or close eye) matches the page; 'may have impaired taste or dry eye' is correctly optional and omitted.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable angioedema from face swelling
rules.problem: Painless swelling of lips or eyes -> Angioedema likely; airway-obstruction line is management and correctly not encoded.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable mumps from painful face swelling
rules.problem: Painful facial swelling with fever, headache and body pain, all required, which matches the page's 'with fever, headache, body pain'.

rules.rule: Urgent: face symptoms with stroke, anaphylaxis, facial cellulitis or kidney disease signs
rules.problem: Red box 'Give urgent attention ... any of' -> Urgent is right; and(face symptom, or(stroke signs, anaphylaxis pattern, active facial cellulitis, active kidney disease)) mirrors the four bullets and the house pattern.

summary: No invented or misplaced content: all 164 conditions trace to page 49 text, all 50 SNOMED concepts exist, and types, triggers, probable/possible levels and the Urgent priority all match the page. The most consequential issue is the sinusitis probable rule requiring all five descriptive features with 'and' (and losing 'headache worse on bending forward'), which will under-fire. Smaller precision losses: 'previous shingles on same side of face' has no side, trigeminal 'superficial' is dropped, and allergen exposure loses the 'within the past few hours' window; forehead-sparing is modelled as (no Upper facial weakness), with Lower facial weakness available as a positive alternative.
